project_and_compatibility.implementation_language: Cucumber.js and playwright-bdd are implemented in TypeScript/JavaScript and run on Node.js. Gherkin feature files contain the executable specifications, while TypeScript or JavaScript step definitions call Playwright APIs. The direct composition uses @cucumber/cucumber plus Playwright as a browser library; the stronger evaluated composition uses playwright-bdd to generate native @playwright/test cases.
project_and_compatibility.node_and_typescript_compatibility: Both current compositions have strong direct compatibility evidence, but repository-specific execution is [uncertain]. @cucumber/cucumber 13.2.1 declares and tests Node 22, 24, and 26 and develops against TypeScript ^6.0.0. playwright-bdd 9.2.0 declares Node >=20, was published with Node 24.16.0, develops against TypeScript 6.0.3, and accepts @playwright/test >=1.44; its maintainer confirmed passing tests with Playwright 1.62. The packages support npm and TypeScript test code without changing the frontend package's module mode. A dedicated E2E directory or package is still preferable, and no install was run with this repository's exact Node 24, TypeScript 6.0.3, and lockfile configuration.
project_and_compatibility.operating_system_support: The Node-based composition runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows. With current Playwright, local supported Linux and GitHub-hosted Ubuntu x86-64 are first-class targets; Playwright also documents supported Ubuntu/Debian arm64 targets. Official Playwright Ubuntu container images are available. Managed Firefox and WebKit require glibc, so Alpine/musl is not a complete three-engine target.
project_and_compatibility.license_and_governance: @cucumber/cucumber, playwright-bdd, and the relevant Playwright packages are MIT or Apache-2.0 licensed and require no commercial license. Cucumber returned to community ownership and now publishes a collaborative governance process with five core team members, consensus or majority decisions, public funding channels, and David Goss as JavaScript core maintainer. playwright-bdd is a personal repository owned and overwhelmingly maintained by Vitaliy Potapov (vitalets), funded through GitHub Sponsors, with no published multi-maintainer governance or succession policy. Microsoft governs and commercially stewards upstream Playwright. All licenses permit repository and CI use subject to their notice terms.
project_and_compatibility.installation_model: Preferred path: npm install -D @playwright/test playwright-bdd, then npx playwright install --with-deps or install selected engines. Configure defineBddConfig, generate native tests with npx bddgen, and run npx playwright test. Direct Cucumber path: install @cucumber/cucumber, Playwright or @playwright/test, and a TypeScript loader such as tsx; implement World and hooks to launch a browser, create a fresh context/page, attach diagnostics, and close resources. The Playwright browser binaries and Linux libraries remain large separate artifacts. A version-matched mcr.microsoft.com/playwright image is optional and does not include the project's npm packages.
project_and_compatibility.candidate_scope_and_layer: BDD composition and abstraction layer, not an independent browser engine. playwright-bdd translates Gherkin scenarios into generated Playwright Test files and retains the integrated Playwright runner. Direct Cucumber.js instead uses Cucumber as the runner and Playwright only as the browser automation library, requiring more lifecycle and artifact code.
project_and_compatibility.authoring_and_async_model: Stakeholder-facing behavior is expressed as Given/When/Then Gherkin scenarios, scenario outlines, tables, doc strings, tags, and backgrounds. Async TypeScript step definitions map text through Cucumber Expressions or regular expressions to awaited Playwright actions and assertions. playwright-bdd supports Playwright-style fixture arguments, Cucumber-style World objects, scoped definitions, scenario/step/worker hooks, and decorators. This introduces a three-layer model: feature text, step matching and shared definitions, then Playwright fixtures/actions. It improves readable behavioral specifications only when product stakeholders review and own the Gherkin; UI-script-like steps merely add indirection and duplicate lifecycle concepts.
project_and_compatibility.build_pipeline_coupling: Black-box tests can target the existing Parcel development server or the production Parcel build served by Gin. Neither composition requires Vite, frontend source transformation, browser-side instrumentation, or a replacement build pipeline. playwright-bdd adds a test-only generation phase that writes .features-gen files before Playwright Test starts. Stable 9.2.0 requires explicit generation; the unreleased 9.3 line adds watch mode, source maps, and generation locks. Generated files should be ignored rather than fed into the application build.
project_and_compatibility.testability_instrumentation_required: No production source transform, injected runtime, special route, or relaxed security policy is required. Playwright can use roles, labels, visible text, IDs, and optional stable test IDs after HTMX swaps. Application-specific deterministic fixture/reset APIs, health endpoints, and a Yahoo Finance substitute may still be justified, but they are not BDD requirements. Gherkin does require a maintained step vocabulary and fixture/World layer in test code; this is significant test-harness instrumentation even though it does not ship in production.

Cucumber 13 changed parallel runtime to worker threads and dropped Node 20, demonstrating meaningful major-version migration risk. playwright-bdd has a detailed changelog but no long-horizon roadmap; v7 removed the Cucumber runner dependency, v9 tightened arity and raised Node requirements, and unreleased v9.3 changes generation and source mapping. [uncertain] There is no published wrapper support lifetime or succession plan, so future compatibility and roadmap continuity depend heavily on one owner.

Cucumber.js 13.2.1 supports Node 24 and 26, uses current Cucumber parser/message packages, and develops against TypeScript 6. playwright-bdd 9.2.0 uses TypeScript 6.0.3 in development, declares Node >=20 and @playwright/test >=1.44, explicitly added Playwright 1.60 and 1.61 support, and passed its suite against 1.62 according to the maintainer. Stable 9.2 still embeds older Cucumber component generations than Cucumber.js 13, because it translates messages rather than running the current Cucumber.js runtime.
maintenance_health.wrapper_upstream_lag: [uncertain] playwright-bdd is sensitive to Playwright internal/reporting changes despite a broad >=1.44 peer range. Its changelog records explicit adaptations for Playwright 1.51, 1.55, 1.60, and 1.61; current 9.2.0 passed Playwright 1.62 tests by 2026-08-04 without requiring a new stable release. This suggests lag of days to several weeks for sampled upstream releases, but no complete historical distribution or compatibility service level was measured. The direct Cucumber.js plus Playwright-library path avoids this translation-wrapper lag but loses Playwright Test runner integration and requires custom lifecycle code.
maintenance_health.maintainer_concentration: [uncertain] Cucumber has public collaborative governance, community funding, and named maintainers across implementations; historical cucumber-js contributions are spread among several major contributors, although JavaScript leadership is currently identified with one core maintainer. playwright-bdd has 17 contributors returned by GitHub's endpoint, but vitalets accounts for 2,037 historical contributions and all ten newest sampled commits, is the only npm maintainer listed, controls releases, and owns the repository. The wrapper therefore has a high practical bus-factor risk even though outside contributions and sponsorship are welcome. Staffing continuity and release-credential succession were not published.

community_adoption.npm_downloads: For the complete seven-day window 2026-08-15 through 2026-08-21, the npm API recorded 2,457,586 downloads of @cucumber/cucumber and 540,138 downloads of playwright-bdd.
community_adoption.github_metrics: [uncertain] Observed 2026-08-22: cucumber/cucumber-js had 5,381 stars, 1,115 forks, 38 combined open issues/pull requests, 32 issue-only open items, and a same-day push. vitalets/playwright-bdd had 763 stars, 92 forks, 31 combined open issues/pull requests, 28 issue-only open items, and a 2026-08-21 push. GitHub's contributor endpoint returned at least 100 entries for Cucumber.js and 17 for playwright-bdd, but exact current contributor and dependency-graph dependent counts were not collected.
community_adoption.ecosystem_usage: Cucumber has a mature cross-language ecosystem, a common Gherkin/message model, official editors and reports, formatters, tag expressions, and long-standing integrations with test management and CI products. playwright-bdd supplies working examples, Cucumber HTML/JSON/JUnit/message adapters, custom formatter support, Playwright projects/fixtures, BrowserStack/Sauce/Currents/TestDino guides, Allure guidance, and a Discord channel. The wrapper's npm volume demonstrates meaningful use, but no independently verified list of organizations running this exact Playwright-BDD composition in production was found. Direct Cucumber-Playwright examples are common but vary substantially in lifecycle quality.
community_adoption.community_support: Cucumber provides extensive official Gherkin and Cucumber.js documentation, GitHub Issues and Discussions, Discord, training material, and a large body of Stack Overflow and third-party guidance. playwright-bdd provides a focused documentation site, examples, GitHub Issues, Discord, migration guides, and Playwright/Cucumber editor integration instructions. Support for the exact composition is narrower than either upstream community, and advice often mixes the direct Cucumber runner with the generated Playwright-BDD runner, so version and architecture must be identified before applying examples.
community_adoption.adoption_trend: Both direct package signals are growing. @cucumber/cucumber rose from 1,485,670 downloads in the aligned Saturday-Friday window 2025-08-16 through 2025-08-22 to 2,457,586 in 2026-08-15 through 2026-08-21, about 65.4 percent. playwright-bdd rose from 97,897 to 540,138 in those aligned seven-day windows, about 451.7 percent, while its repository remained active. This is a strong growth signal for package acquisition, not proof of active stakeholder participation or unique production projects.
community_adoption.adoption_metric_normalization: The metrics are separate and must not be added. @cucumber/cucumber measures the broad JavaScript Cucumber runner across API, integration, and browser-testing uses; it does not identify Playwright compositions. playwright-bdd more directly measures the evaluated generated-runner layer, but downloads can include repeated CI installs, upgrades, mirrors, bots, and transitive use. Both comparisons use complete aligned Saturday-Friday UTC windows one year apart. Playwright's much larger upstream usage is not attributed to the BDD wrapper.

browser_and_runtime_coverage.browser_engines: With Playwright, both compositions can drive managed Chromium, patched Firefox, and patched WebKit. Chromium projects can also target installed Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge channels. Stock Firefox and native Safari are not driven by Playwright. The Gherkin layer does not expand browser coverage; playwright-bdd maps scenarios to normal Playwright projects, while direct Cucumber code must implement its own browser matrix and launch policy.
browser_and_runtime_coverage.browser_protocol: Browser control uses Playwright's client/server protocol and patched browser integrations, not WebDriver or WebDriver BiDi. Chromium-only CDP attachment is available but lower fidelity than the normal Playwright connection. Cucumber and playwright-bdd operate above this layer and do not make tests protocol-portable.
browser_and_runtime_coverage.headless_and_headed_modes: Playwright supports default headless CI execution and headed local debugging for all managed engines. playwright-bdd inherits --headed, --debug, UI Mode, slow motion, Inspector, and Xvfb behavior from Playwright Test. Direct Cucumber must expose launch options through profiles, environment variables, or World parameters and wire pause/debug behavior itself.
browser_and_runtime_coverage.browser_version_management: Playwright package versions select tested browser revisions installed by npx playwright install; upgrades normally require reinstalling matching browsers. Teams can install only selected engines, set the browser cache path, use branded Chromium channels, or pin a version-matched official image. Cucumber.js and playwright-bdd do not manage browsers independently, so package-lock and browser/image versions must be coordinated across three layers.
browser_and_runtime_coverage.parallel_browser_support: playwright-bdd inherits Playwright projects, project selection, workers, fullyParallel, and --shard, and its Cucumber report adapter represents project/browser metadata. Direct Cucumber.js supports worker-thread parallelism and native sharding, but browser matrices and report merging require profiles or CI matrices plus custom setup. Database-sensitive scenarios can be kept at one Playwright worker or constrained through Cucumber's custom parallel assignment, while browser projects run separately.
browser_and_runtime_coverage.mobile_emulation: Playwright device descriptors and context options provide viewport, screen, user-agent, touch, mobile mode, device scale, locale, and related emulation. playwright-bdd fixtures can derive those options from projects or tags. This is responsive emulation in desktop browser engines, not testing on physical Android/iOS devices or native mobile Safari.
browser_and_runtime_coverage.real_browser_fidelity: Managed Chromium can be supplemented with installed Chrome/Edge channels. Playwright Firefox is patched and Playwright WebKit is an upstream WebKit build, not branded Firefox or Apple Safari. Ubuntu WebKit does not reproduce Safari packaging, codecs, operating-system integration, or release timing. Native Safari remains outside this stack and requires a separate Safari/WebDriver or cloud path if it becomes mandatory.
browser_and_runtime_coverage.environment_determinism_controls: The preferred playwright-bdd path exposes Playwright fixtures for locale, timezone, viewport, screen, device scale, user agent, geolocation, permissions, color scheme, contrast, reduced motion, offline state, storage state, and clock control. Screenshot assertions can disable animations and mask/style volatile regions. Gherkin tags can select fixtures but should not duplicate configuration logic. Random-number and backend-time determinism remain application or fixture responsibilities.

application_fit.dynamic_dom_synchronization: Strong browser-layer fit. Playwright locators reacquire DOM nodes before each action, actionability checks retry, and web-first assertions poll, which handles HTMX replacement and lazy Handlebars rendering when step definitions assert the post-swap state. Gherkin adds no automatic HTMX awareness; step authors must avoid fixed sleeps, generic prose such as 'the page is ready', and retained element handles. Reusable business-level steps can centralize correct state-based synchronization, but overly generic steps can hide it.
application_fit.routing_support: Navigo History API routing is ordinary browser behavior for Playwright. Steps can navigate directly to Gin-served deep links, assert URLs and route-specific DOM, and exercise back/forward/reload. playwright-bdd retains page.waitForURL and web-first URL assertions. Feature text should describe route-visible behavior rather than implementation details; cleanup and listener behavior still require explicit scenarios and assertions.
application_fit.locator_model: Step definitions have the complete Playwright locator model: role, label, text, placeholder, alt text, title, CSS, and configurable test IDs, with strict single-target actions and reacquisition after HTMX swaps. Feature files should not contain CSS selectors or unstable IDs. A small domain vocabulary mapped to accessible locators improves stakeholder readability; a large generic click/fill step catalog transfers brittle selectors into Gherkin and weakens both readability and type safety.
application_fit.form_interaction: Playwright fill, clear, press, pressSequentially, focus, blur, check, select, keyboard, pointer, and native validation APIs remain available in async steps. This can exercise input masks, HTMX validation, focus/blur, hidden-value synchronization, and dynamic allocation/history rows realistically. Scenario outlines and data tables express representative input combinations, but complex tables can become a second data DSL and should not replace typed fixture builders for low-level setup.
application_fit.canvas_and_download_support: Chart.js can be checked through visible labels/legends, source data or chart state evaluated in the page, canvas dimensions, and a narrowly stabilized screenshot assertion. playwright-bdd inherits Playwright's snapshot workflow and download events, including filename, stream/path, saveAs, failure, and payload parsing. Direct Cucumber must configure snapshot comparison and download directories itself. Gherkin should assert business meaning and exported payload content; pixel-level details belong in step implementation and reports.
application_fit.network_and_api_access: playwright-bdd steps and fixtures can use APIRequestContext for REST seeding/cleanup and Playwright routing, HAR, request/response events, waitForResponse, fulfill, abort, continue, and fetch. Browser-originated Yahoo Finance traffic can be intercepted; server-side Gin calls require a configured backend stub or mock service. Direct Cucumber can use the same library APIs but must construct request contexts and teardown manually. Feature files should state external-service behavior without embedding fixture endpoints.
application_fit.same_origin_support: Both compositions can test the consolidated production Gin origin or Parcel port 8000 with its existing /api proxy and need no CORS relaxation. baseURL is a normal Playwright project/fixture option in playwright-bdd. Direct Cucumber can pass the URL through World parameters or environment configuration.
application_fit.test_isolation: The preferred composition inherits a fresh Playwright BrowserContext and page per generated scenario/test, isolating cookies, storage, IndexedDB, permissions, and tabs. Cucumber-style World can itself be a test-scoped Playwright fixture. Direct Cucumber requires explicit Before/After hooks to create and close one context per scenario. PostgreSQL remains external to browser isolation; use unique per-worker data, disposable databases/schemas, deterministic reset, or one worker for shared state.
application_fit.external_server_model: Both paths can point at any independently started application through baseURL, World parameters, or environment variables. playwright-bdd does not require Playwright webServer ownership, so the same features can target Parcel development, production-like Docker Compose, or another reachable deployment. Environment-specific behavior should remain in fixtures/configuration rather than conditional Gherkin.
application_fit.application_lifecycle: playwright-bdd inherits Playwright webServer, project dependencies, global setup/teardown, and worker/test fixtures, but adds a required bddgen phase before discovery. It still cannot declaratively complete this repository's full build, Docker Compose, Flyway, Gin readiness, PostgreSQL reset, backend-log collection, and volume disposal without repository code. Direct Cucumber provides BeforeAll/AfterAll and coordinator hooks but needs even more custom process management. Cancellation-safe Docker cleanup belongs in an always-running CI step, not only a BDD hook.
application_fit.visual_regression_workflow: playwright-bdd retains Playwright Test's first-party screenshot baselines, update workflow, per-project paths, masks, styles, animation disabling, thresholds, pixel limits, and CI diffs. Gherkin can expose a concise outcome such as 'the allocation chart matches the approved view', while baseline paths and tolerances remain code/configuration. Pin browsers, fonts, viewport, timezone, data, and Chart.js animation completion. Direct Cucumber does not receive this integrated snapshot lifecycle from the Playwright library alone and would need a separate comparator/harness.
application_fit.accessibility_audit_integration: The preferred path is compatible with the documented open-source @axe-core/playwright integration and Playwright role/name assertions and ARIA snapshots. Reusable fixtures or steps can attach axe results to Playwright and Cucumber reports. Accessibility scenarios can be stakeholder-readable, but broad 'page is accessible' steps should retain detailed violation evidence and cannot replace manual assessment. Direct Cucumber can call axe-core but must assemble reporting itself.

reliability.waiting_model: playwright-bdd preserves Playwright actionability checks, locator assertion polling, navigation/URL waits, event and network waits, expect.poll, and fixture/test timeouts inside each step. The BDD layer adds step and hook boundaries but not additional browser waiting. Direct Cucumber has step timeouts and hooks but relies on Playwright library calls for waiting. Correct steps should await user-visible state or a specific response; fixed delays and broad network-idle waits remain unreliable for HTMX.
reliability.flake_controls: The preferred composition inherits Playwright retries, immediate/isolated retry strategies, assertion/action/navigation/test timeouts, --repeat-each, --last-failed, worker replacement, trace-on-retry, and failOnFlakyTests. Tags can apply special timeout/retry behavior. Cucumber.js independently supports scenario retries with fresh Worlds, retry tag filters, rerun files, random order, and custom parallel assignment. Do not combine both runners' retry models in one path. playwright-bdd issue 395 records that Cucumber HTML formatters still await upstream retry-information support, so Playwright reports should remain the authoritative flake view.
reliability.isolation_model: Each generated Playwright scenario is a normal test with a fresh BrowserContext; fixtures and World are test scoped, while browser and worker fixtures are reused by scope. BeforeAll/AfterAll aliases are worker hooks, not once-per-suite hooks. The wrapper recommends another package for exactly-once cross-worker caching, which should not be used as a substitute for database isolation. Direct Cucumber also creates a fresh World per scenario/retry but needs explicit context teardown.
reliability.resource_usage: [uncertain] Relative to direct Playwright Test, the preferred path adds Gherkin parsing, bddgen output, Cucumber message/report packages, source/generated files, and step-level report data; v9 limited generation concurrency to half the CPUs after memory pressure in constrained CI. Browser workers, three engines, traces, video, screenshots, and HTML attachments remain the dominant cost. Direct Cucumber may reuse one browser per worker but must manage it safely. No repository benchmark measured install size, generation time, peak memory, CPU, disk, or scenario duration.
reliability.parallelism_controls: playwright-bdd uses Playwright worker count, fullyParallel, serial groups, projects, dependencies, and shards. Generated scenarios can be tagged/configured, but PostgreSQL safety is still external; start state-mutating E2E execution with one worker, then use per-worker databases or unique data before increasing concurrency. Direct Cucumber has an additional setParallelCanAssign API that can prevent simultaneous scenarios by tag, plus worker IDs and native shards. The direct path offers finer BDD-specific assignment but requires custom browser and report orchestration.
reliability.flake_observability: Playwright HTML/JSON/JUnit/blob/custom reports classify first-attempt pass, retry pass/flaky, and final failure; traces can retain the first failure or retries and failOnFlakyTests can enforce policy. playwright-bdd maps scenarios and steps into those reports and can also emit Cucumber formats, but Cucumber HTML retry representation is currently incomplete. There is no open-source built-in long-term quarantine registry or historical dashboard; tags, JSON/JUnit retention, and repository-owned trend processing are required.

diagnostics_and_developer_experience.failure_artifacts: playwright-bdd automatically carries Playwright screenshots, video, traces, console/network trace evidence, attachments, and HTML output into generated scenario results; its Cucumber HTML reporter can embed or externally store screenshots, video, and traces. Cucumber JSON skips large attachments by default. Direct Cucumber can call this.attach and Playwright tracing/screenshot/video APIs but must implement capture and flushing in hooks. Neither path automatically captures Gin, PostgreSQL, Flyway, or Docker logs.
diagnostics_and_developer_experience.debugging_tools: The preferred path inherits headed mode, Inspector, page.pause, UI Mode, Trace Viewer, browser DevTools, Node debugging, and the official Playwright VS Code extension. Stable 9.2 exposes generated .features-gen tests in the extension; direct run/debug from original .feature gutter locations and source-mapped HTML locations are unreleased 9.3 capabilities as of observation. Direct Cucumber supports Node debugging and feature-line execution but lacks Playwright Test UI/fixture integration unless custom tooling is added.
diagnostics_and_developer_experience.test_generation: bddgen deterministically generates Playwright tests from existing Gherkin and step definitions; it is a compiler step, not a recorder that discovers meaningful behavior. Missing-step snippets and bddgen export help maintain the vocabulary. Playwright codegen can record browser actions for implementation, but cannot design stakeholder-quality Gherkin or reusable domain steps. playwright-bdd offers an optional agent skill and prompt-generation feature; generated specifications and code still require human review.
diagnostics_and_developer_experience.reporters: playwright-bdd supports all normal Playwright reporters, including console, HTML, blob, JSON, JUnit, GitHub, and custom reporters. Its adapter additionally emits Cucumber HTML, JSON, JUnit, message/NDJSON, and some custom Cucumber formatters, with project metadata and automatic attachments. Four Cucumber message types are not yet emitted, and some custom formatter constructor objects are fake. Shard blob reports can be merged into Cucumber output. Direct Cucumber supplies progress/summary/HTML/JSON/JUnit/message/rerun/custom formatters but does not natively supply Playwright's trace-oriented report integration.
diagnostics_and_developer_experience.documentation_quality: Cucumber.js documentation is extensive and current for configuration, Gherkin support code, World, hooks, parallelism, sharding, retries, formatters, attachments, ESM, and TypeScript. playwright-bdd documentation is unusually thorough for a community wrapper and covers fixtures, hooks, generation, tags, reports, projects, authentication, IDEs, migration, and examples. The stable docs branch and main/upcoming docs can diverge: watch mode and source maps are documented on main but were still 9.3 beta, so users must verify the pinned version. Upstream Playwright documentation remains the source for most browser behavior.
diagnostics_and_developer_experience.local_workflow: Stable workflow is npx bddgen followed by npx playwright test. Developers can select generated tests by file/title/grep/tag/project, use headed/debug/UI mode, inspect reports/traces, and run bddgen --tags. The official Playwright extension discovers generated tests, while Cucumber extensions provide Gherkin completion/navigation. Stable 9.2 requires regeneration after feature changes and generally exposes generated files for run/debug; 9.3 beta adds watch, locks, source maps, and original-feature gutter actions. This is measurably more ceremony than direct Playwright Test.
diagnostics_and_developer_experience.failure_log_correlation: Playwright timestamps actions, BDD steps, assertions, console and network entries, and attachments in one scenario/test trace; Cucumber reports retain feature/scenario/step identity. Custom fixtures can attach browser errors and failed responses with testInfo. The workflow must separately timestamp and collect Gin, Flyway, PostgreSQL, and Compose logs using a shared run, shard, worker, and scenario identifier. Generated-file paths and original feature paths should both be preserved until stable source maps are adopted.
diagnostics_and_developer_experience.artifact_data_exposure: Screenshots, videos, traces, HTML/JSON/message reports, HAR/network bodies, console output, storage state, downloads, feature example tables, and World attachments can expose credentials and portfolio data. playwright-bdd Cucumber reports can embed binary artifacts; external attachments reduce report size, not sensitivity. Its optional Fix with AI creates a prompt attachment containing the error, Gherkin, code, and ARIA snapshot but does not itself call a model. Use synthetic data, skip unnecessary attachments, sanitize logs, restrict retention/access, never commit auth state, and keep AI prompts and external model use disabled in CI.

github_actions_fit.official_ci_support: There is no dedicated official Cucumber-Playwright or playwright-bdd GitHub Action. The preferred path follows official Playwright guidance: setup Node, npm ci, install version-matched browsers with --with-deps or use a pinned image, run bddgen, then run Playwright Test and upload reports. playwright-bdd maintains its own Linux/Windows CI and passed Playwright 1.62 in GitHub Actions. Cucumber documents CI sharding generically. This is viable on ubuntu-latest but adds one generation step and another package compatibility boundary.
github_actions_fit.browser_caching: Use setup-node's npm cache for lockfile dependencies. Playwright does not generally recommend caching browser binaries because restoration can cost as much as download and Linux packages are separate; installing selected engines or pinning the official image is simpler. If cached, key by OS, architecture, and exact Playwright version. Gherkin and generated test files are small and should normally be regenerated, not shared as mutable cross-job cache state.
github_actions_fit.artifact_integration: Low effort on playwright-bdd: configure Playwright/Cucumber reporters and capture paths, then upload playwright-report, cucumber-report, blob reports, and selected test-results with actions/upload-artifact under an always/failure policy. Cucumber HTML can externalize large attachments and blob reports can merge across shards. Backend and Compose logs still need explicit workflow collection. Apply short retention and restricted access because both feature examples and browser artifacts may contain portfolio data.
github_actions_fit.sharding_and_matrix_support: playwright-bdd inherits Playwright --shard and browser projects/matrices. Each shard emits a blob report; an aggregation job downloads blobs and runs playwright merge-reports with the Playwright config to produce Playwright or Cucumber reports. bddgen must use the same config and should run deterministically before each shard. Direct Cucumber 13 supports shard INDEX/TOTAL plus in-process parallel workers, but cross-job report aggregation is less integrated. Database-mutating shards require separate databases/schemas or must remain unsharded.
github_actions_fit.container_compatibility: The stack can run directly on ubuntu-latest beside this repository's Docker Compose services, or in a version-matched Playwright Ubuntu image. If the test runner is containerized, the application must be reachable through service DNS or a host-gateway mapping because localhost is container-local; Chromium benefits from --init and adequate shared memory. Cucumber/playwright-bdd add no browser container. Pin Node packages, image/browser versions, and architecture together.
github_actions_fit.failure_cleanup: Playwright Test fixtures close pages, contexts, browsers, and owned webServer processes; direct Cucumber must close them in After/AfterAll even after failures. Hard timeout or cancellation can interrupt BDD hooks. Docker Compose, PostgreSQL volumes, generated files, and backend processes therefore need job-level cleanup guarded by if: always(), unique Compose project names, disposable volumes, and explicit process termination. Preserve logs before docker compose down.

cost_and_risk.open_source_completeness: All required baseline capabilities are open source: Gherkin parsing and execution, Playwright browser automation/Test runner, Chromium/Firefox/WebKit builds, fixtures, waiting, retries, workers, sharding, screenshots, visual snapshots, video, traces, HTML/JSON/JUnit/message reports, axe integration, and local debugging. No paid service is required. The direct Cucumber path needs more custom code to reach the same diagnostics, while playwright-bdd delivers them through Playwright Test.
cost_and_risk.optional_cloud_dependency: No cloud is mandatory. Cucumber Reports publishing, BrowserStack/Sauce grids, Currents/TestDino dashboards, Allure services, commercial visual review, and model providers are optional. Local Playwright/Cucumber HTML, trace viewing, committed visual baselines, GitHub artifacts, JUnit/JSON, and repository-owned trend processing provide non-cloud alternatives, though they do not supply a turnkey long-term analytics dashboard.
cost_and_risk.migration_cost: Moderate to high. Feature text is portable in principle, especially when it describes domain behavior, and TypeScript/Playwright actions remain familiar. In practice the suite depends on Gherkin structure, step-expression matching, shared vocabulary, tags, generated tests, playwright-bdd fixtures/hooks/report translation, Playwright locators, and visual baselines. Moving to direct Playwright requires flattening scenarios into tests; moving to direct Cucumber requires replacing Playwright Test fixtures and artifacts. Generic reusable steps can create hidden coupling and make migration or refactoring harder than duplicated explicit tests.
cost_and_risk.security_and_supply_chain: [uncertain] @cucumber/cucumber 13.2.1 and playwright-bdd 9.2.0 npm metadata include registry signatures, trusted GitHub Actions publishing, and SLSA provenance attestations. Cucumber runs dependency automation, CodeQL, and workflow security analysis; playwright-bdd uses automated publishing and recorded npm-audit fixes. The composition adds Cucumber parser/report packages and the wrapper to Playwright's browser-download and npm supply chain, and generated steps execute with host, browser, database, and network access. No complete vulnerability, license, install-script, container, or transitive-provenance audit was performed, and no repository-specific SECURITY.md was found for the wrapper. Pin lockfiles/images, use npm ci, scan dependencies, restrict CI permissions/egress, and review generated artifacts.
cost_and_risk.custom_harness_burden: High relative to direct Playwright Test. playwright-bdd supplies generation, Gherkin matching, Playwright fixtures, browser lifecycle, reports, and attachments, but the repository must maintain feature conventions, step definitions, fixture/World typing, generation scripts, source/generated-file policy, version coordination, and BDD-specific IDE guidance. It also still needs Compose/Flyway/Gin readiness, deterministic PostgreSQL setup/reset, Yahoo Finance replacement, backend log collection, artifact redaction, and cancellation-safe teardown. Direct Cucumber adds custom browser/context lifecycle, traces, video, visual baselines, and report wiring on top of that.
cost_and_risk.capability_delivery_tier: Core upstream Cucumber: Gherkin, expressions, World, hooks, tags, retries, parallelism, sharding, attachments, and Cucumber reports. Community wrapper playwright-bdd: generated Playwright tests, fixture integration, BDD hooks/tags, project mapping, and Cucumber report adapters. Core Playwright Test: browser management, locators, waiting, isolation, API/network controls, projects, retries, workers, sharding, snapshots, downloads, traces, video, screenshots, reports, UI Mode, Inspector, and codegen. Separate open-source integration: axe-core and optional Allure/global-cache tools. Custom repository code: application/database lifecycle, service mocking, log correlation, deterministic Chart.js checks, artifact policy, and stakeholder vocabulary governance. Paid cloud: none required.
cost_and_risk.ai_execution_boundary: Deterministic Gherkin parsing, bddgen generation, Playwright execution, assertions, retries, and CI require no LLM, AI credential, inference cost, or model egress. playwright-bdd's agent skill is optional authoring assistance. Fix with AI only generates a local report attachment until a human sends it to a model, but that prompt can contain errors, source, Gherkin, and an ARIA snapshot. Keep AI options disabled in required CI and require all feature and step changes to run without AI.

evidence_and_decision.confidence: High confidence in licenses, versions, package requirements, Node/TypeScript development versions, npm downloads, GitHub snapshots, Gherkin lifecycle, generation architecture, Playwright inheritance, report formats, and documented CI capabilities because they use first-party repositories, documentation, registry data, and live APIs. Medium confidence in application-fit, adoption interpretation, issue health, wrapper lag, and governance risk. Low confidence in resource use, complete supply-chain status, final weighted score, and repository-specific behavior because no spike or benchmark was executed.
evidence_and_decision.hard_gate_result: CONDITIONAL PASS [uncertain]. Pass through playwright-bdd: open-source TypeScript/JavaScript E2E composition; Node 24 and TypeScript 6 development evidence; Linux/GitHub Ubuntu; Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit; black-box Parcel/Gin operation; HTMX-safe Playwright locators/waits; Navigo routing; realistic forms; canvas and downloads; REST seeding and network interception; fresh browser contexts; configurable base URL; headed/headless modes; retries, workers, shards, visual snapshots, traces, videos, reports, and no mandatory cloud/AI. Conditions: run exact repository installation; generate before test discovery; keep Gherkin behavioral and stakeholder-owned; add Compose/Flyway/PostgreSQL lifecycle and Yahoo stub; prove artifact redaction; and complete the required application spike. Direct Cucumber.js plus Playwright passes browser capability gates but fails the low-custom-harness expectation unless substantial lifecycle, diagnostics, and visual-report code is accepted.
evidence_and_decision.deal_breakers: No confirmed browser or runtime incompatibility. Exclude the composition if stakeholders will not actively review or co-own Gherkin, because then step indirection and duplicate lifecycle concepts have cost without the stated benefit. Other exclusion triggers are refusal to depend on a high-bus-factor wrapper, a requirement for native Safari on Ubuntu, zero generated test files, one-layer debugging, or zero custom application/database lifecycle code. A failed Node 24/TypeScript 6/application spike or unacceptable wrapper lag on a pinned Playwright release would also be a deal breaker.
evidence_and_decision.project_fit_score: 84.0/100 provisional [uncertain]. Weighted calculation: application fit 84/100 x 30% = 25.20; maintenance 84/100 x 20% = 16.80; reliability 84/100 x 15% = 12.60; adoption 85/100 x 15% = 12.75; GitHub Actions experience 88/100 x 10% = 8.80; diagnostics 85/100 x 5% = 4.25; cost and risk 72/100 x 5% = 3.60; total 84.00. Playwright's capabilities and strong package growth score well. Deductions reflect generation/step indirection, stable source-map lag, incomplete Cucumber retry reporting, wrapper concentration, coordinated upgrades, and additional repository harness/governance work. No project spike or resource benchmark validates the score.
evidence_and_decision.recommendation: Viable alternative, not the default recommendation [uncertain]. Select playwright-bdd only if product stakeholders will continuously write or review concise behavioral Gherkin and the team accepts ownership of the step vocabulary. It preserves nearly all Playwright Test capability and has strong recent adoption, current TypeScript 6 evidence, rich Cucumber reporting, and active development. Direct Playwright Test remains simpler, better governed end to end, easier to debug, and lower maintenance for an engineering-owned E2E suite. Do not choose the direct Cucumber.js runner merely for Gherkin: it gives up integrated Playwright fixtures, lifecycle, UI Mode, visual workflow, and automatic artifacts unless the repository rebuilds them.
evidence_and_decision.empirical_project_spike_result: Not performed [uncertain]. No Cucumber, playwright-bdd, Playwright, feature, step, fixture, generated test, browser binary, report, or CI workflow was added or executed. Required proof: install the stable packages on repository Node 24 and TypeScript 6; generate and run one scenario from editor and CLI; verify HTMX node replacement/lazy loading, Navigo deep links and history, focus/blur/native validation and dynamic rows, deterministic Chart.js semantic plus visual checks, download payloads, API fixtures, server-side Yahoo replacement, PostgreSQL reset and one-worker safety; force a retry/failure; inspect Playwright and Cucumber traces/reports plus backend/Flyway/Compose logs; verify sensitive-data controls and guaranteed teardown; and measure generation/runtime/resource overhead against direct Playwright Test.
